Strait of Gibraltar Holy War Vanguards
RagShortTexts: Berber lancers wielding oryx-hide adarga shields formed the swift desert vanguard of the.

Variants.Content: The Zenata Berber warriors of the Marinid Sultanate and their loyal Black Guard reshaped North African warfare from the Moroccan steppe. Their weapons were hard, heart-shaped adarga bucklers of oryx hide and slender light lances. Riding Barb stallions, they manoeuvred around the heavier Christian cavalry rather than meeting it head-on. Their mobility let them raid, screen, and pursue, and the sultan's household troops gave the dynasty a dependable force at court. The style of war they brought to the Iberian frontier made Marinid armies a serious factor in the region around the Strait of Gibraltar.

Marinid sultans controlled trans-Saharan gold caravans, and that revenue paid for professional retinues pledged to holy war. Those retinues were readied for incursions across the Strait of Gibraltar to defend Moorish Andalusia. A lord who depended on the sultan's favour had to read the caravan tolls and the muster lists side by side, since both showed where the money was going.

Adarga shields of cured antelope hide deflected arrows under the desert sun. Berber lancers did not lock knee to knee with the enemy. They swirled like dust devils around the heavy line, skewering gaps in the armour. Carry light, keep moving, and never let a Christian knight hold you still. Water was the first thing a rider counted before every charge.
